summary: Core dumps are disabled persistently for node1’s local service accounts while systemd-coredump continues recording crash metadata without storing core payloads. Reboot persistence and full node recovery were verified.
actions_performed: Set PAM soft and hard core limits to 0 for local service-account UIDs 1–999.
Set systemd’s default service core limit to 0.
Configured systemd-coredump with Storage=none and ProcessSizeMax=0.
Tested an intentional crash as the chrony service account before and after reboot.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed, services recovered, and policy remained effective.

evidence.requirement: Disable core dumps for local service accounts
evidence.summary: PAM, systemd defaults, and the running chronyd process all show soft/hard core limits of 0; the post-reboot crash stored zero core files.
A UID 995 process aborted after reboot; systemd-coredump logged the event and coredumpctl cataloged it with COREFILE=none.
Configuration hashes remained unchanged after reboot, log-only settings were loaded, and live PAM/systemd process limits remained 0/0.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 953e6cb5-ce48-44db-bc5a-32edac59aac5; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; node1 returned with boot ID 1f557440-ac1e-446c-814c-a4c91d9390e9, all required services active, no failed units, synchronized time, and SSH listening.
